comment: What both clients say about the site lens library, held to the same bytes: the Python client (steerlab_server.client.lens_transfer, Server/tests/test_lens_transfer.py) and the Mac (LensLibrary.swift, LensLibraryTests.swift). Every value is fictional.

unavailable.pushReason: The engine at http://runner.example.invalid:8080 does not offer a lens library (its capabilities do not report lensLibrary.available as true). Nothing was sent.
unavailable.pushRepairAction: Give the engine a lens library folder it can write (on a cluster, the site profile's lensLibrary folder; on any other engine, STEERLAB_LENS_LIBRARY_ROOT), then run the command again. An engine from before the lens library must be updated first.
unavailable.archiveReason: This archive refers to its lens instead of carrying it, and the engine at http://runner.example.invalid:8080 does not offer a lens library (its capabilities do not report lensLibrary.available as true). Nothing was sent.
unavailable.archiveRepairAction: Package the request without --lens-reference so it carries its lens, or give the engine a lens library folder it can write (on a cluster, the site profile's lensLibrary folder; on any other engine, STEERLAB_LENS_LIBRARY_ROOT) and upload the request again. An engine from before the lens library must be updated first.

externalTransfer.reason: The engine at http://runner.example.invalid:8080 does not accept file transfers over HTTP, so this client cannot send the lens's bytes. Nothing was sent.
externalTransfer.repairAction: Copy runs/jlens-lenses/custom-lens-example/jacobians.safetensors to the site with the site's own transfer tool, then run lens-push again with --adopt <the path of that copy on the site>: the site checks the copy against the lens's hash and keeps it.

interrupted.repairAction: Run the command again: it sends only what the site still lacks.

purposes.lensReference: With --lens-reference, a request that names a lens refers to the copy in the site's lens library and leaves the lens file out; send the lens once with lens-push first.
purposes.lensCopy: Copy a lens from another workspace on this machine into this one, under the same name and record. Reviews by default and writes nothing; repeat with the --plan-sha256 the review shows to copy it. Each file is checked before and after, and on macOS the copy is a clone that uses no extra disk space where the filesystem allows. A lens already here under that name is not copied again; its converted file is put back if it is missing. The answer lists any other names under which this workspace holds the same lens.
purposes.lensPush: Send a workspace lens to the site's lens library once, in parts that follow its layers, each checked, and register its record there. Sends only what the site lacks, so it can be run again after an interruption. With --adopt, the site checks and keeps a copy already on it, and nothing is uploaded.
purposes.lensStatus: Report whether the site's lens library holds a workspace lens and whether the site has its record. Reads only.
purposes.artifactImport: Import the reviewed instrument into the workspace. A lens is named from its reviewed files, so importing the same files again finds the same lens, and puts its converted file back if it is missing.

copyArguments.lensID: science lens-copy takes one lens ID: the name of the lens's folder under runs/jlens-lenses/ in the workspace that holds it.
copyArguments.from: science lens-copy needs --from <workspace directory>: the workspace that holds the lens.
